videos.description:
The reason you are underpaid has nothing to do with your competence — it is a scarcity problem you have been broadcasting in the wrong direction for years. Perceived scarcity is the only mechanism that sets your price, and every time you made yourself effortlessly available, you taught the market exactly what you were worth. This is not career advice. This is a structural analysis of how value is actually assigned to human beings — the architecture that Machiavelli documented five centuries ago and that most channels will never touch because it indicts the viewer as much as the system. The full mechanism is below, and it reorganizes everything.

WHAT THIS VIDEO COVERS
By the end of this video, you will understand why effort without strategic positioning is invisible to every market you operate in. You will see the exact mechanism — rooted in Machiavelli's observations and confirmed by behavioral psychology research — that separates who does the work from who captures the value. Your understanding of availability, generosity, and professional loyalty will be permanently restructured. You will stop confusing being necessary with being valued. These are not the same condition, and they do not produce the same price.

MECHANISM BREAKDOWN
THE WRONG GAME — The market does not reward competence; it rewards perceived scarcity, and you have been playing a game whose actual rules were never explained to you.
THE COOKIE JAR EXPERIMENT — Worchel, Lee, and Adewole proved in 1975 that identical objects become more valuable the moment supply contracts, and your career has been the jar of ten cookies.
THE BORGIA MECHANISM — Cesare Borgia installed a man to do his brutal work, captured every benefit, then executed him in the town square — and this architecture operates in every organization you have ever belonged to.
THE COST OF ALWAYS BEING THERE — Persistent availability is not read as generosity; it is encoded as baseline, and no one has ever experienced your absence enough to feel what they would lose.
MIDDLE PATH FAILURE — Machiavelli watched princes who tried to please every faction get categorized as safe, forgettable, and replaceable — the professional equivalent of the man who never says no.
THE SCOREBOARD YOU'VE BEEN IGNORING — The person who got what you deserved was not playing "be the best"; they were playing "be the only," and those are two entirely different games.
THE POSTURE OF THE PRINCE — Maximinus, emperor of Rome, destroyed himself not through incompetence but through the visible effort of proving he deserved to be there.
THE GENEROSITY TRAP — Unconditional generosity does not build loyalty; it builds expectation, and expectation unfulfilled becomes resentment, not gratitude.
LOYALTY WITHOUT LEVERAGE — Every unopened door needs to wonder what is behind it; when you remove all friction of access, you remove the signal that sets your price.

WARNING / POSITIONING
This video does not tell you to work harder. It tells you why working harder inside the wrong structure will never change your price. The distinction between being necessary and being valued is not comfortable, and the people who reject it will continue making unconscious pricing decisions about themselves for years. Clarity and comfort have never been the same offering.
